title: categories.by_slug
description: Resolve slugs to root->leaf ancestry. This object validates the request payload; the response is a flat mapping {"<slug>": ["<root_id>", ..., "<leaf_id>"]} — see $defs.Path. It is categories.path keyed by slug: the segments are category IDS (as strings) on the way out, so a consumer feeds the last one straight back into categories.features, whose payload is typed as an integer id. A slug with no row is simply absent from the mapping, mirroring the projections read() convention — absence is what a consumer turns into its own refusal, and it is never an error, an empty list or a null. An inactive category still answers (a listing can sit in a category retired after publication); a soft-deleted one does not.

slugs.description: Slugs to resolve. Category.slug is unique across the whole tree, so one slug is a complete address.

Path.description: One response value: the named category's own ancestry, root first and the category itself last. A root category answers a single-element path.
